name: Cabazitaxel plus a concurrent steroid (mCRPC, post-docetaxel)

biomarkers.note: Cytotoxic taxane chemotherapy is not biomarker-restricted. Castrate testosterone (below 50 ng/dL) must be maintained with ongoing ADT. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, Systemic Therapy for M1 CRPC (PROS-18) and Discussion.

lineOfTherapy: category 1, preferred taxane option after exposure to docetaxel and an ARPI in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (post-docetaxel)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with a docetaxel-containing regimen (and typically a prior ARPI), on ongoing ADT
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, Discussion, prostate line 7451 to 7456 (CARD; cabazitaxel category 1 preferred after docetaxel and an ARPI); PROS-18 (Cabazitaxel category 1, Post-ARPI/Post-Docetaxel), prostate line 1779

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: ongoing ADT (orchiectomy, LHRH agonist, or LHRH antagonist)

drugs.name: Cabazitaxel

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate line 7454 (CARD: cabazitaxel at 25 mg/m2 with concurrent steroid); prostate line 7463 (PROSELICA compared 20 mg/m2 with 25 mg/m2; panel recommends 20 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for fit patients, 25 mg/m2 for healthy patients opting for more aggressive treatment)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion, prostate lines 7454 and 7463. Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m2 IV on day 1 of a 21-day cycle with a concurrent daily steroid (TROPIC/CARD approved dose). ALTERNATIVE lower dose: 20 mg/m2 every 3 weeks is source-recommended as the preferred starting dose for fit patients (PROSELICA noninferior for overall survival, less toxicity; prostate line 7463); both 20 and 25 mg/m2 are source-stated starting doses. A biweekly 16 mg/m2 regimen with prophylactic G-CSF is a source-stated option for patients 65 years or older (CABASTY, prostate line 547).

premedications.name: Premedication for cabazitaxel (hypersensitivity)
premedications.notes: Prophylactic antihistamine, H2 antagonist, and corticosteroid before infusion per labeling (prostate lines 7466 to 7468); specific doses not enumerated in the provided extract.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Provide per emetogenic-risk tier on the day of chemotherapy.

supportiveCare: concurrent steroid: cabazitaxel should be given with concurrent steroids (daily prednisone or dexamethasone on the day of chemotherapy) per prostate line 7466; the specific corticosteroid milligram dose is not enumerated in the provided extract, so the steroid is described here rather than modeled as a dosed drug (no invented dose).
continue ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G).
cycles null: standard is every 3 weeks; total cycle count is individualized (not fixed in the provided extract).

G-CSF: prophylactic white-blood-cell growth factor per current guidelines, particularly in this heavily pretreated population (higher febrile-neutropenia risk); mandatory with the 16 mg/m2 biweekly option.

monitoring: CBC before each cycle (high neutropenia/febrile-neutropenia risk)
PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, or grade 3 or higher diarrhea
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and dose-reduce cabazitaxel per labeling (e.g., 25 to 20 mg/m2); add or intensify G-CSF; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: cabazitaxel improves survival in mCRPC after docetaxel (TROPIC); PROSELICA established noninferiority of 20 mg/m2 versus 25 mg/m2

guideline.locator: PROS-18 (Cabazitaxel category 1, Post-ARPI/Post-Docetaxel), prostate line 1779; Discussion (TROPIC/CARD cabazitaxel 25 mg/m2 with concurrent steroid, prostate lines 7454, 7422; PROSELICA 20 vs 25 mg/m2 and panel-recommended 20 mg/m2 for fit patients, prostate line 7463; concurrent steroid requirement, prostate line 7466; CABASTY 16 mg/m2 biweekly for age >= 65, prostate line 547)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for cabazitaxel plus a concurrent steroid in post-docetaxel metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (disease #54 mCRPC). The cabazitaxel dose (25 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, the TROPIC/CARD approved dose) is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate lines 7454, 7422); the source-recommended lower starting dose of 20 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for fit patients (PROSELICA noninferior) and the 16 mg/m2 biweekly option for patients 65 or older (CABASTY) are captured in the drug note (prostate lines 7463, 547). The mandatory concurrent steroid (daily prednisone or dexamethasone) is source-stated (prostate line 7466) but its milligram dose is not enumerated in the provided extract, so it is described in supportiveCare rather than modeled as a dosed drug (no dose invented, no VERIFY). cycleLengthDays 21 is source-stated; cycles is null (individualized). Ongoing ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL is required. No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
